headline: Lynx Rescued from War-Torn Ukraine Feels Grass Under Her Paws
meta_description: A Eurasian lynx illegally kept as a pet in Kyiv was rescued during wartime and evacuated to safety in England, where she experienced grass for the first time.
summary_short: Ursa, a Eurasian lynx found ill in war-torn Kyiv, was rescued and flown to a UK sanctuary where she finally walked on grass and rolled in the sun.
body:
A Eurasian lynx named Ursa, rescued from illegal captivity in Kyiv, took her first steps on grass this week—rolling joyfully onto her back—at the Big Cat Sanctuary near Ashford, Kent. Found seriously ill in January after being kept as a private pet, Ursa was initially cared for at a Ukrainian wildlife rescue centre while bombs fell around the capital. The Big Cat Sanctuary in England raised £134,000 to fund what staff described as a "high risk" evacuation mission through active combat zones and complex border crossings. After arriving safely in Britain in February, Ursa spent months in a temporary enclosure while her new home was being built. This week's debut on the grass marked a turning point: the specially constructed, nature-filled enclosure was finally complete.

"To see Ursa take her first steps here in Kent was an incredibly emotional moment for the whole team," said Cam Whitnall, managing director of The Big Cat Sanctuary. "This mission was fraught with unpredictability, navigating a war zone with a vulnerable apex predator, but seeing her safe makes every risk worthwhile." The sanctuary now houses Ursa alongside other rescued wild cats, including another Eurasian lynx called Rhys, a Bobcat named Blob, and a Fishing cat named Boson.

For Ursa, the rescue represents far more than relief from neglect—it signals hope for conservation efforts. Staff emphasized that combining world-class welfare with modern facilities secures a sustainable future for smaller wild cat species globally. After spending her life under the shadow of conflict, Ursa has finally found her forever home.
quick_facts: Eurasian lynx named Ursa found ill in Kyiv, Ukraine in January
Big Cat Sanctuary in Kent raised £134,000 for her evacuation
Rescued through war zone and border crossings in high-risk mission
Evacuated to England in February, now lives with other rescued cats
Walked on grass for the first time this week in new enclosure
